topic: sub:12|Network flow|Network flow terms: source, sink, capacity

solutions.latex:
The capacity of a cut is the sum of the capacities of the pipes that cross the cut from the source side to the sink side.

Cut 1 crosses pipes $e$, $g$, $f$ and $d$.

Pipe $f$ is directed from the sink side back towards the source side, so it is not counted.

Pipes $e$, $g$ and $d$ all flow towards the sink side, so they are counted.

$$\text{Capacity} = e + g + d$$
This matches option C.

solutions.latex:
The degree of $F$ is the number of edges at $F$.
$$\therefore\ 3$$

The outflow at $C$ is the total of the flows on the edges directed out of $C$.
$$\therefore\ 6$$

solutions.latex:
The cut capacity is the sum of the capacities of the edges crossing the cut in the forward direction.
$$\begin{aligned} 8+11+x &= 30 \\ 19+x &= 30 \\ x &= 11 \end{aligned}$$
The 8 on the lower right is ignored, as it crosses the cut in the opposite direction.
$$\therefore\ x=11$$
